additions.description: Provides a GET /password-recovery-html/{email} endpoint returning HTML content for password recovery token
additions.reasoning: The specification requires password recovery email sending but does not mention any endpoint returning HTML content for password recovery.

additions.description: Returns HTML content as a string inside a JSON 'message' field in the /password-recovery-html/{email} endpoint
additions.reasoning: The specification does not require or mention returning HTML content in the response body for password recovery; it only requires sending an email.

additions.description: Uses urllib to send password recovery emails to a local mailcatcher service at http://localhost:1080/messages
additions.reasoning: The specification requires that a password recovery email is sent and verified via mailcatcher, but the code explicitly implements sending via HTTP POST to mailcatcher, which is an implementation detail not required by the specification.

omissions.description: GET /items/{item_id} does not check that the requesting user has permission to read the item; any authenticated user can read any item
omissions.reasoning: The specification requires that a user cannot read an item owned by another user (returns 400 with 'Not enough permissions'), but the code returns the item without permission checks.

omissions.description: GET /items/ returns all items without filtering or restricting to the current user's items when the user is not a superuser
omissions.reasoning: The specification implies that normal users should only see their own items, but the code returns all items regardless of ownership.

omissions.description: POST /items/ does not verify that the user is authenticated before creating an item
omissions.reasoning: The specification requires authentication for item creation; the code depends on current_user but does not explicitly handle unauthenticated requests with proper error messages.

omissions.description: POST /users/signup returns 400 with detail 'User with this email already exists' instead of the exact message 'The user with this email already exists in the system' as required by the specification
omissions.reasoning: The specification requires the exact error message for duplicate user registration, but the code uses a different message.

omissions.description: POST /users/ (private user creation) does not restrict access to superusers only; the code requires superuser but the specification requires this explicitly
omissions.reasoning: The code correctly restricts this endpoint, so no omission here.

omissions.description: PATCH /users/me/password does not check that the new password is different from the current password before hashing
omissions.reasoning: The code raises HTTP 400 if new password equals current password, so no omission here.

omissions.description: DELETE /users/me allows deletion of normal users but forbids superusers from deleting themselves, matching specification
DELETE /users/{user_id} allows only superusers to delete users and forbids superusers from deleting themselves, matching specification
POST /items/{item_id} update and DELETE /items/{item_id} enforce permission checks consistent with specification
POST /login/access-token returns 400 with detail 'Incorrect email or password' on failed login, matching specification
GET /api/v1/users/not-a-uuid and GET /api/v1/items/not-a-uuid return 422 validation errors for invalid UUID format, matching specification
Password and email length and format validations are implemented as required by the specification
Password recovery for non-existent user returns 404 with appropriate detail message
Reset password endpoint validates token and password length, returns 400 or 422 as appropriate
User update endpoints enforce unique email constraints and return 409 with correct detail message
User deletion and item deletion endpoints verify existence and permissions, returning 404 or 403 or 400 as specified
User cannot update another user's profile unless superuser, enforced with 403 error
User cannot read another user's profile unless superuser, enforced with 403 error
User cannot update password to the same as current password, enforced with 400 error
User cannot delete themselves if superuser, enforced with 403 error
User cannot create a new user unless superuser, enforced with 403 error
